extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, peer reviewers, authors, and members of the Council of Science Editors (CSE)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the role and processes of the CSE Editorial Policy Committee in drafting, reviewing, and publishing editorial and publishing policies for scientific journals and books, including stakeholder input, Board review, member comment, and final approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of topics addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee studies and analyzes procedural, ethical, legal, and economic policies and recommends policies and/or guidelines that relate to the editing, review, and publication of manuscripts in books and journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas of the peer review scientific publication process that are controversial and poorly defined are priorities; the committee aims to address such problems by drafting policies in these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of policy statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide guidance and a framework for discussion among editors, publishers, peer reviewers, and authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies are intended as guidance and a basis for discussion rather than unilateral rules; they serve as references for the editorial community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee identifies topics that could benefit from a policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification is proactive—committee looks for issues in the publishing process that lack clear or accepted practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting with broad input
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members draft a policy with input from as many sources as they can identify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit diverse perspectives and evidence during drafting to inform balanced, well-founded policy language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Board review and tentative approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft is forwarded to the Board of Directors for preliminary review. The Board gives tentative approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board's tentative approval allows the draft to be published for wider scrutiny while not yet final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of draft for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft is published in Science Editor and on the website for review and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public posting solicits member and community feedback to improve and validate the draft policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of member suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Member suggestions are incorporated into a final draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback from members is actively used to revise drafts before final Board review; some policy statements undergo review-and-comment cycles prior to finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Board review and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The final draft is again reviewed by the Board, approved, and published in final form to serve as a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after Board approval is a policy published as final guidance for the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to formal review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a specific 'Policy for Review and Approval of Statements Drafted by the Editorial Policy Committee' describing the review and approval process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal documented process governs how committee statements are reviewed and approved; drafts follow this established procedure.
